whatItDoes: Shows how inflation changes the purchasing power of money over time. Enter an amount, an annual inflation rate, and a number of years to see both the future numeric value and today's purchasing power.
whyItExists: Inflation erodes what money can buy, so a fixed amount loses value over time. Seeing that shift is essential for long-term savings, retirement planning, and setting realistic financial goals.
whoShouldUse: Anyone planning long-term savings or retirement, comparing prices over time, or budgeting for future costs.
useCases: Estimate how much today's money is worth in the future
Plan retirement income in terms of purchasing power
See how a fixed amount loses spending power over decades
Model the 'future cost' of today's prices
instructions: Enter the annual inflation rate as a percent
Read the loss in purchasing power and the future equivalent
examples: $1,000 at 3% for 10 years -> future value +34%, buying power falls about 26%
$50,000 at 3% for 30 years -> future value $121,363, buying power today $20,600
bestPractices: Use a long-run average rate for planning, usually around 3%
Remember inflation varies over time and by region
Apply the real return (after inflation) when comparing investments
Re-run the calculation when rates or time horizons change
commonMistakes: Confusing the future numeric value with purchasing power
Using a short-term spike in inflation for a long projection
Forgetting that salaries and prices usually both rise with inflation
Ignoring that some costs (healthcare, housing) outpace the average
faq: Why does the same amount buy less? — Inflation raises prices each year, so money goes less far.
What does future value mean? — The projected numeric amount after applying the rate.
What is today's value? — The amount today that purchases the same as the future value then.
Is my data shared? — No, everything runs locally in your browser.
